data: My family’s fished this lake for generations, and I want it to keep supporting our village. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That leaves 50 tons, which doubles back to 100—so each of us can earn $10,000 a month without draining the lake. Let’s agree to that limit and review everyone’s catches together each month. John, would you be willing to join that agreement?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons for me. My family taught me to leave enough fish for next month, and this gives all five of us a steady living. Let’s check the catches together each month and talk through any problems before we fish again. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. A steady income matters more to my family than one big catch that leaves the village struggling later. If someone needs extra in a particular month, let’s discuss it beforehand and agree on offsets so our combined catch stays at 50 tons. Jack, will you join us?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here from my family, and I want the lake to keep feeding our village. Kate’s idea of agreeing on offsets makes sense—any extra for one person needs to come out of someone else’s share, not next month’s stock. John, are you willing to keep to 10 tons with us?

I’m in for 10 tons. That gives us all a fair living while leaving the lake healthy for our families and the village. We’ve all agreed now—let’s stick to it and compare catches at the end of the month. Any changes should be agreed together before we fish, with the total kept at 50 tons.
